body:
Forgejo now takes sign-ins with GitHub accounts, so issues and pull requests go there. Until now the README and CONTRIBUTING sent people to GitHub, which is only a read-only mirror.

What the docs now say:
- A new account waits for a maintainer to activate it.
- New accounts can't create repositories, so there are no forks. Pull requests are AGit pushes: `git push origin HEAD:refs/for/main -o topic=…`, made from a Forgejo clone over HTTPS with an access token.
- CI skips AGit pull requests, because the runners are trusted with release credentials (the guard from #3). A maintainer opens the change again from a branch here to run the full suite.

The push syntax was checked on a private repo, where it opened an AGit pull request (flow=1).
head: refs/pull/2/head
title: docs: send issues and pull requests to Forgejo

body:
Forgejo treats an AGit pull request (pushed to `refs/for/main`, no fork needed) as untrusted and holds its runs for approval, but its payload reports this repository as the head (`head.repo.full_name == github.repository`), so the existing fork gate let it through. When a maintainer acts on an outsider's PR (reopen), Forgejo 17 runs this branch's workflows, with secrets, against the PR's commit (services/actions/trust.go). Outside contributors are about to be able to sign in with GitHub and open AGit PRs, so the gate now also requires `github.event.pull_request.flow == 0`.

Proof (throwaway SisyphusMD/agit-guard-proof-20261116): an AGit PR's payload has `flow=1` and head repo = base repo, and the gated job was skipped (run 37485); a branch PR has `flow=0` and the gated job ran (run 37486).

Outside PRs get CI when a maintainer, after reading the diff, pushes the head to a branch here.

The condition is folded to stay under yamllint's 120-character limit.

body:
Closes #7

The rules ask for coverage, and nothing measured it for the blueprint: a branch could go untested without anyone noticing. Now a whole-suite test run fails unless every branch in the blueprint is taken by some test.

How: `tests/branch_coverage.py` lists the blueprint's branches from its YAML (each trigger by index, both outcomes of every `if`, each `choose` option plus "nothing matched", and each `condition` step passing and stopping). `conftest.py` keeps every automation run's Home Assistant trace and records the step paths and outcomes each test took. At the end of a full run, any branch nothing took is listed by blueprint line and the run fails. A run that cannot be judged (paths given, tests deselected or failed, collect-only) says "Blueprint branch coverage NOT checked" and why, so it never looks like a pass. A "nothing matched" outcome counts only from a run that finished, not one stopped mid-step. `repeat`, `parallel`, `while` and `until` raise, so a new construct cannot slip past uncounted.

It found two real gaps, both now tested: an overload that clears while power is high but drops within the start delay, on a paused job and on an unplugged appliance (`test_power_that_falls_within_the_start_delay_after_a_trip_clears_*`). Each new test fails when its condition is forced.

Proof it fails: with `test_a_sensor_that_does_not_cut_power_resumes_once_it_clears` skipped, both floor (2024.10) and latest (2026.10) exit 1 with `line 475: action/2/choose/9/sequence/1 condition passing` and "59 of 60 branches taken". Unmodified, both print "All 60 blueprint branches taken." with 100 passed.
